Advancements in technology and treatment modalities for cancer, act as a driving force for the increase in the cost of cancer care. As there will be a tangential increase in cancer burden for the state, our health system must be prepared to keep up with the newer technology along with maintenance of the existing facilities. All these necessitate the development of a selfsustainable cancer care model in Tamil Nadu. An expert committee will be formed to derive a strategy for a Self-Sustainable Health care Model for cancer-related services in Tamil Nadu.

10.3.1. Smart Investment in Innovation

Smart investments in cancer care are the need of the hour which can help in;

• Improving patient outcomes • Alleviating demands on healthcare systems • Improving sustainable access to cancer care

A few areas for possible investments are;

• Artificial Intelligence aids in screening, diagnosis, and patient follow-up • Digitalisation of Health • Precision Medicine & Biomarker Testing • Curative therapies • Out-of-hospital care

10.3.2. Providing Autonomy to State Apex Centre for Cancer Care

To strengthen the quantity and quality of cancer care services, the State Apex Institute needs the autonomy, flexibility, and freedom

• The State Apex Institute should be made an autonomous institution under the Tamil Nadu Government with administrative and functional autonomy like TMH in Mumbai and adequate funding support. The establishment of a regular budget line to the apex center is recommended. • The State apex institute would serve as the official technical advisory body to the Government of Tamil Nadu and play as a Nodal and networking agency within and outside the State • The State Apex Institute will constitute a Scientific Council that will advise the Director on matters related to Clinical and scientific/evidence-based services. It will have representation from in-house members and others from outside the state or country based on the need. • The State apex institute will also take the lead in forming a State level Cancer Consortium which will meet at least annually by networking with all the oncologists in the state from regional and tertiary cancer care centers to provide them a platform for deliberating on the issues in cancer

management updating on the development in the field of diagnostics and treatment etc. • The Director of the Institution should be a highly qualified and experienced oncologist identified by a competent selection committee constituted by the Government. The Director may be selected by inviting applications from qualified candidates who will be interviewed by the selection committee in a competitive selection process. Based on the recommendation of the selection committee, the Government may appoint the Director for a term of five years with one-year probation.

The No Objection Certificate (NOC) for a Certificate of Registration (RC) is a formal document issued by the Regional Transport Office (RTO) that declares the RTO has no objection to the vehicle being transferred, re-registered, or moved to another jurisdiction. i. Low NOC applications Due to Procedural Complexity

Due to procedural complexity and lack of clarity in the NOC application process for Registration Certificate (RC), citizens have been reluctant to initiate updates. Multiple forms, clearances, and supporting documents are being requested, often with overlapping or unclear specifications.
